A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neural Harmonic Textures by the same authors. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, references, and complete supplementary material are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis, joint RGB/semantic reconstruction, and HDR image-fitting results, including quantitative comparisons and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies and adds BBSplat comparisons, training-time measurements, preprocessing sensitivity results, and training trajectories.

M1.justification: The architecture, feature interpolation, harmonic encoding, deferred decoding, and application adaptations remain unchanged. The documented radiance-field loss weighting changes: the SSIM coefficient decreases from 0.2 to 0.1 and scale regularization from 0.01 to 0.005 (v1 Table 14; v3 supplementary Table 12), a limited revision of the existing objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use MipNeRF360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending for scene reconstruction, retain joint RGB/LSEG reconstruction, and evaluate the same 15-image HDR dataset. The added analyses use existing scenes and tasks; preprocessing and primitive-budget variations change protocols rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: BBSplat, already cited in v1, becomes an evaluated comparator in v3 supplementary Table 1 across five primitive budgets, with equal-primitive and approximately equal-memory comparisons. The comparator sets in the retained main benchmark, semantic, and HDR experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The high-quality MipNeRF360 outdoor configuration changes from 4.5M primitives and 20k iterations to 5M and 25k. Several reported learning rates and loss coefficients also change. v3 introduces preprocessing comparisons, BBSplat budget controls, training trajectories, and hardware-specific timing protocols. It explicitly documents JPEG references for main Table 1 and default gsplat downsampling elsewhere; v1 did not specify this distinction. These are substantial protocol revisions and additions, without establishing that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds reference-preprocessing sensitivity analysis, training/overfitting curves for bicycle and room, and a qualitative bonsai comparison at 10K primitives. Existing optimization, encoding, architecture, feature-dimension, semantic, and compression ablations remain. The encoding ablation moves from v1 main Table 4 to v3 supplementary Table 11 with unchanged results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The new training curves contain no uncertainty bands, and additional averages retain the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 substantially expands results with BBSplat quality/storage/speed comparisons, training times, preprocessing sensitivity, and training curves. Main Table 1 replaces NHT's MipNeRF360 results of 29.01/0.840/0.212 with 28.74/0.834/0.216 and revises three baseline rows; changed settings prevent interpreting this as a same-setting performance decline. Table 3 changes Triangle Splatting+NHT LPIPS from 0.190 to 0.227 and updates the 3DGUT+NHT row. Controlled Table 2, semantic results, and HDR results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The rendering equations, harmonic decoder formulation, barycentric interpolation derivations, Clough–Tocher construction, gradient estimation, and densification mathematics are retained. Supplementary equations are renumbered, with no added or substantively revised definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: primitive-anchored harmonic features, one deferred neural decoding pass, strong real-time reconstruction, compatibility with multiple primitive types, and semantic/HDR applications. Added comparisons do not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting overfitting to training epochs relative to dataset size and attributing preprocessing-related metric differences to JPEG artifacts. It newly qualifies Triangle Splatting results as an unoptimized proof of concept. It also asserts superior quality over BBSplat at equal primitive counts, although the new table shows a PSNR–LPIPS tradeoff.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link advertised as providing source code and further results. It documents reference-image processing, shared baseline regularization, BBSplat skybox allocation, storage precision, and A100/RTX 5090 measurement hardware, alongside revised hyperparameter values. The PDFs establish these disclosures, not the external availability or contents of the linked code.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds discussion and citations for Neural Point-Based Graphics, TRIPS, Neural Point Catacaustics, Feature Splatting, NeuMesh, and SurRF. It also expands the distinction from already-cited BBSplat and Textured Gaussians. This improves positioning against local-feature and deferred-decoding predecessors while retaining the broader research framing.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites expand related work, clarify optimization attribution and evaluation settings, and refine application descriptions. The supplement gains its own title block and separate numbering, replacing lettered appendix sections. Most prose and the main narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds supplementary Tables 1, 2, and 5 and Figures 1–2. It relocates the encoding ablation, repositions existing displays, moves table captions above their tables, and adjusts highlighting and spacing. Existing method diagrams and principal qualitative comparisons are retained; the presentation receives additions and reformatting rather than a wholesale redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 improves evaluation transparency through explicit preprocessing protocols, a relevant BBSplat comparison, measured training costs, and additional diagnostic analyses. Expanded related work and code-access information also help readers assess and reproduce the work. The gain is limited by overbroad interpretation: supplementary Table 1 shows worse NHT LPIPS at every equal-primitive budget despite claims of uniformly higher quality. Overall, the added evidence and clearer documentation provide a modest net improvement.
